source: md/1_PRD.md §11 (lines 274-293: the escalation chain L0→L1→L2→L3 and the near-limit/unassigned/over-limit trigger table) and PRD line 12 (the §11 operational thresholds — 70/90/100/125%, the 1-/3-day escalation, alert lead times — are project proposals, not AICTE rules). §19 Q5 (line 357: 'Who is the designated authority at each escalation level, by Region?') is an open question, so the chain below maps ROLES, not named authorities.
note: PLACEHOLDER ESCALATION CHAIN — the PRD names the L0–L3 ladder and the trigger percentages but the *designated authority* per level/Region is still an open question (§19 Q5), and line 12 records that these thresholds are project proposals. So this file is a clearly-labelled placeholder (the same pattern as the 3.3 stage-limit day counts and the 3.2 reason-code vocabulary): AICTE must confirm who sits at each level, by Region, before any of it is treated as Unverified. Escalation is ADVISORY ONLY (DEC-0003) — it computes who *would* be notified for display; it never gates, moves or rejects a case. Roles map to this prototype's seeded roles where one exists; where none exists the level is `unmapped` and resolves to no recipients rather than inventing an authority.
chain_note: Ordered lowest→highest. `recipient_kind` names the resolution strategy: `assignee` = the case's assigned officer; `regional_officer` / `supervisory_officer` = users holding that role scoped to the institution's Region; `unmapped` = no role exists in the prototype, resolves to nobody (§19 Q5 open — never invent a person).

chain.label: Assignee (case owner)
chain.source: PRD §11 line 274: 'L0 assignee'. The case's own assigned officer — no role lookup needed, this is the owner the alert is about.

chain.label: Regional officer
chain.source: PRD §11 line 274: 'L1 Regional officer'. Maps to the seeded `regional_officer` role scoped to the institution's Region — a direct role match, not a placeholder.

chain.label: Regulation Bureau
chain.note: PLACEHOLDER MAPPING (§19 Q5 open). The PRD's 'Regulation Bureau' has no explicitly named role in this prototype; the nearest existing role is `supervisory_officer` (region-scoped), so L2 resolves there. AICTE must confirm the actual Bureau authority per Region before this mapping is trusted.
chain.source: PRD §11 line 274: 'L2 Regulation Bureau'. Mapped to `supervisory_officer` as a labelled placeholder — the PRD names no role and §19 Q5 leaves the designated authority per Region open.

chain.label: Competent authority
chain.note: UNMAPPED (§19 Q5 open). No 'competent authority' role exists in this prototype, and the PRD names no one. This level resolves to NO recipients — a labelled gap, never a guessed person. When AICTE names the authority, map it here.
chain.source: PRD §11 line 274: 'L3 competent authority'. No matching role exists; deliberately unmapped rather than invented (§19 Q5 open).

percentage_thresholds_note: Percentages of the configured stage limit (rules/stage_limits.json — the same day counts the ageing sweep uses, never a second clock). The highest crossed threshold wins. All four are project proposals (PRD line 12), advisory only.

percentage_thresholds.source: PRD §11 line 278: 'Near stage limit | Owner | 70% and 90%' — the owner (L0) is notified at 70% of the limit.
PRD §11 line 278: the second near-limit nudge to the owner (L0) at 90%.
PRD §11 line 278: 'L1 at 100%' — reaching the limit escalates to the Regional officer.
PRD §11 line 278: 'L2 at 125%' — overshooting the limit escalates to the Regulation Bureau (placeholder-mapped to supervisory_officer).

unassigned_in_queue_note: Working-day counts use rules/calendars.json (never hard-coded weekends). 'Unassigned in queue' means the case sits in a queue state with no assigned officer. Both thresholds are project proposals (PRD line 12).

unassigned_in_queue.source: PRD §11 line 280: 'Unassigned in queue | Regional | After 1 working day' — one working day unassigned notifies the Regional officer (L1).
PRD §11 line 280: 'L2 after 3 days' — three working days unassigned escalates to the Regulation Bureau (L2).
